weeks.title: Q2: W1 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to understand and solve division problems with a remainder using the array and area models.
sc: I can solve a division problem with and without a remainder using the area model.
I can solve a division problem using an array and the area model.

days.lo: I am learning how to understand and solve two-digit dividend division problems with a remainder in the ones place by using place value disks.
sc: I can model division with place value disks
I can relate my work on the place value chart to long division.
I can check my quotient and remainder with multiplication and addition.

days.lo: I am learning how to represent and solve division problems requiring decomposing a remainder in the tens.
sc: I can divide two-digit numbers by one-digit numbers using place value disks, regrouping in the tens.
I can relate the model to the steps in the algorithm.
I can check my quotient and remainder with multiplication and addition.

days.lo: I am learning how to find whole number quotients and remainders.
sc: I can divide a two-digit number by a one-digit divisor with a remainder in the tens place.
I can divide with a remainder in the tens and ones places using the division algorithm.
I can use mental math to divide and calculate a remainder.

weeks.title: Q2: W2 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to solve division problems without remainders using the areamodel.
sc: I can solve division problems without remainders.
I can solve division problems without remainders using the area model.

days.lo: I am learning how to divide multiples of 10, 100, and 1,000 by single-digit numbers.
sc: I can rewrite expressions in unit form.
I can represent division expressions using place value disks.
I can decompose units using place value disks and divide.
I can solve for division of multiples of 10, 100, and 1,000

days.lo: I am learning how to represent division problems that include decomposing a remainder in the hundreds place.
sc: I can represent division expressions using place value disks.
I can decompose units using place value disks and divide.
I can relate division using place value disks to the standard algorithm.

days.lo: I am learning how to represent and solve three-digit dividend division with divisorsof 2, 3, 4, and 5.
sc: I can represent division expressions using place value disks.
I can decompose units using place value disks and divide.
I can relate division using place value disks to the standard algorithm.

days.lo: I am learning how to represent numerically four-digit dividend division with divisorsof 2, 3, 4, and 5, decomposing a remainder up to three times.
sc: I can divide using the standard algorithm and multiply to check the answer.
I can divide using the standard algorithm and decompose units as necessary.
I can represent a division problem using a strip diagram.

weeks.title: Q2: W3 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to solve division problems with a zero in the dividend or with a zero in the quotient.
sc: I can divide with a zero in the dividend
I can divide with a zero in the quotient.
I can check my solutions with multiplication.

days.lo: I am learning how to interpret and find whole number quotients and remainders to solve one-step division word problems with larger divisors of 6, 7, 8, and 9.
sc: I can represent what I know and what I need to know with a strip diagram.
I can apply the same division strategy for small divisors to larger divisors.
I can explain what the remainder represents.

days.lo: I am learning how to interpret and find whole number quotients and remainders to solve one-step division word problems with larger divisors of 6, 7, 8, and 9.
sc: I can represent what I know and what I need to know with a strip diagram.
I can apply the same division strategy for small divisors to larger divisors.
I can explain what the remainder represents.

days.lo: I am learning how to explain the connection of the area model of division to the long division algorithm for three- and four-digit dividends.
sc: I can represent long division problems using the area model
I can decompose dividends using number bonds to solve long division problems.
I can explain the connection of the area model of division to the long division algorithm.

weeks.title: Q2: W4 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to multiply two-digit multiples of 10 by two-digit numbers usinga place value chart.
sc: I can use the associative property to rewrite multiplication expressions.
I can represent the expression on a place value chart.
I can multiply using a place value chart.
I can use the distributive property to multiply without a place value chart.
I can relate the associative and distributive property when multiplying.

days.lo: I am learning how to multiply two-digit multiples of 10 by two-digit numbers usingthe area model.
sc: I can represent multiplication expressions with an area model.
I can find the partial products using the area model.
I can relate an area model to the vertical method.

days.lo: I am learning how to multiply two-digit by two-digit numbers using four partial products.
sc: I can use the distributive property to represent and solve two-digit by two-digit multiplication.
I can use an area model and partial products to solve.
I can use partial products to solve and verify with an area model.
I can find the partial products and solve, without using an area model.

days.lo: I am learning how to transition from four partial products to the standard algorithm for two-digit by two-digit multiplication.
sc: I can represent multiplication expressions with an area model showing four partial products.
I can compose one factor in the area model and then solve using only two partial products.
I can solve using two partial products without an area model.
days.note: Lessons combined: teach Lesson 33 in its entirety and include Problems 3 & 5 from Lesson 34 Problem Set; do the Application Problem from Lesson 34.

weeks.title: Q2: W5 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, and angles and recognize them in various contexts and familiar figures.
sc: I can draw, identify, and label points, a line segment, and a line.
I can draw, identify, and label rays and angles.
I can draw, identify, and label points, line segments, and angles in a familiar figure.
I can analyze a familiar figure.

days.lo: I am learning how to use right angles to determine whether angles are equal to, greater than, or less than right angles and draw right, obtuse, and acute angles.
sc: I can fold paper to create a right angle
I can determine whether angles are equal to, greater than, or less than a right angle.
I can draw right, acute, and obtuse angles.

days.lo: I am learning how to identify, define, and draw perpendicular and parallel lines.
sc: I can define perpendicular and parallel lines.
I can identify perpendicular lines by measuring right angles with a right angle template.
I can recognize and write symbols for perpendicular and parallel segments.
I can draw perpendicular and parallel line segments.

days.lo: I am learning how to identify, define, and draw perpendicular and parallel lines.
sc: I can define perpendicular and parallel lines.
I can identify perpendicular lines by measuring right angles with a right angle template.
I can recognize and write symbols for perpendicular and parallel segments.
I can draw perpendicular and parallel line segments.

days.lo: I am learning how to use a circular protractor to understand a 1-degree angle as 1/360 of any circle and explore benchmark angles using the protractor.
sc: I can reason about the number of turns necessary to make a full turn with different fractions of a full turn.
I can Use a circular protractor to measure four quarter turns.
I can measure and draw benchmark angles with the protractor.
I can draw an angle less than 180° using a 180° protractor.

weeks.title: Q2: W6 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to use a circular protractor to understand a 1-degree angle as 1/360 of any circle and explore benchmark angles using the protractor.
sc: I can reason about the number of turns necessary to make a full turn with different fractions of a full turn.
I can use a circular protractor to measure four quarter turns.
I can measure and draw benchmark angles with the protractor.
I can draw an angle less than 180° using a 180° protractor.

days.lo: I am learning how to measure and draw angles, sketch given angle measures, and verify with a protractor.
sc: I can measure angles less than 180° using a circular and 180° protractor.
I can measure an angle greater than 180° by subtracting from 360°.
I can measure an angle greater than 180° by adding on to 180°.
I can recognize turning angles in relation to a clock, a room and various contexts.

days.lo: I am learning how to decompose angles using pattern blocks.
sc: I can derive the angle measures of an equilateral triangle.
I can verify the equilateral triangle’s angle measurements with a protractor.
I can derive the angle measure of unknown angles, and verify with a protractor.

days.lo: I am learning how to use the addition of adjacent angle measures to solve problemsusing a letter for the unknown angle measure.
sc: I can use benchmark angle measures to show that angle measures are additive.
I can demonstrate that the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts.

weeks.title: Q2: W7 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to recognize lines of symmetry for given two-dimensional figures.Identify line-symmetric figures, and draw lines of symmetry.
sc: I can recognize folded symmetry.
I can identify lines of symmetry in familiar figures.
I can draw lines of symmetry.

days.lo: I am learning how to analyze and classify triangles based on angle measure.
sc: I can discover the attributes of various triangles.
I can classify triangles by angle measure.
I can define a triangle.
I can classify triangles by side length.

days.lo: I am learning how to define and construct triangles from given criteria.
sc: I can construct an obtuse triangle.
I can construct a right triangle

weeks.title: Q2: W8 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to classify quadrilaterals based on parallel and perpendicular linesand the presence or absence of angles of a specified size.
sc: I construct and define trapezoids.
I can construct and define parallelograms.
I can construct and define rectangles.
I can construct and define squares.

days.lo: I am learning how to reason about attributes to construct quadrilaterals on square or triangular grid paper.
sc: I can construct a rhombus on a triangular grid.
I can construct a rectangle on a triangular grid.
I can construct non-rectangular parallelograms on a rectangular grid.

days.lo: I am learning how to decompose fractions as a sum of unit fractions using stripdiagrams.
sc: I can write decompositions of fractions represented by strip diagrams as number sentences.
I can draw decompositions of fractions from number sentences using strip diagrams.
days.note: Lessons combined: Fluency and Application Problem from Lesson 1; Concept Development Problems 1-3 from Lesson 1 and Problems 2-3 from Lesson 2; differentiate Problem Set and Exit Ticket based on student data.

weeks.title: Q2: W9 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to decompose unit fractions using area models to showequivalence.
sc: I can draw an area model to illustrate that two fractions are equivalent.
I can decompose a fraction and represent an equivalent fraction in an area model  as the sum and product of unit fractions.
I can model equivalent fractions and represent the decomposition as the sum and product of unit fractions.

days.lo: I am learning how to decompose fractions using area models to show equivalence.
sc: I can use an area model to show that two fractions are equivalent.
I can draw an area model to represent the equivalence of two fractions, and express the equivalence as the sum of unit fractions.
I can decompose to create equivalent fractions by drawing an area model and then dividing the area model into smaller parts.

days.lo: I am learning how to use the area model and multiplication to show the equivalence of two fractions.
sc: I can determine that multiplying the numerator and denominator by the same factor results in an equivalent fraction.
I can determine an equivalent fraction for the area selected, given an area model.
I can express an equivalent fraction using multiplication, and verify by drawing an area model.

days.lo: I am learning how to use the area model and division to show the equivalence of twofractions.
sc: I can compose the shaded fractions into larger fractional units.
I can express the equivalent fractions in a number sentence using division.
I can explain how to use an area model and division to show the equivalence of two fractions.

days.lo: I am learning how to explain fraction equivalence using a strip diagram and the number line, and relate that to the use of multiplication and division.
sc: I can use a strip diagram and number line to find equivalent fractions for halves, fourths, and eighths.
I can use a number line, multiplication, and division to decompose and compose fractions.
I can decompose a non-unit fraction using a number line and division.
